Direction B, built out.

One list, expand in place. Children indent under their group; the row carries the group chip, the roles that change behaviour, how many rules feed it, transaction count and month spend.

Expanding gives you the name, the grouping, merge/archive/delete, the rules that pick it, and the roles with what each one actually does.

Added since the sketch: archived categories (toggle in the toolbar), an empty state, per-rule last-used, and the numbering below.

Sample data — clickable.

The one thing B hid, now fixed.

First match wins, so order decides the answer. Merchant rules are exact and always run first — they show "—" because nothing about their order is a choice. Text rules are numbered in the order they run.

That keeps the tradeoff you accepted (rules live with their category) without leaving the ordering invisible.
A — list + detail. Not chosen; kept for reference.
